source.name: sp_UpsertProducts
source.sourceDefinition:
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.sp_UpsertProducts
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;

    BEGIN TRANSACTION;

    -------------------------------------------------
    -- Update existing products
    -------------------------------------------------
    UPDATE p
    SET
        ProductName = s.ProductName,
        Price = s.Price,
        StockQuantity = s.StockQuantity
    FROM dbo.Products p
    INNER JOIN dbo.ProductImportStaging s
        ON p.SKU = s.SKU;

    -------------------------------------------------
    -- Insert new products
    -------------------------------------------------
    INSERT INTO dbo.Products
    (
        ProductName,
        SKU,
        Price,
        StockQuantity
    )
    SELECT
        s.ProductName,
        s.SKU,
        s.Price,
        s.StockQuantity
    FROM dbo.ProductImportStaging s
    LEFT JOIN dbo.Products p
        ON p.SKU = s.SKU
    WHERE p.ProductID IS NULL;

    -------------------------------------------------
    -- Delete removed products
    -------------------------------------------------
    DELETE p
    FROM dbo.Products p
    LEFT JOIN dbo.ProductImportStaging s
        ON p.SKU = s.SKU
    WHERE s.SKU IS NULL;

    COMMIT TRANSACTION;
END;

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE dbo.sp_UpsertProducts()
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    -------------------------------------------------
    -- Update existing products
    -------------------------------------------------
    UPDATE dbo.Products p
    SET
        ProductName = s.ProductName,
        Price = s.Price,
        StockQuantity = s.StockQuantity
    FROM dbo.ProductImportStaging s
    WHERE p.SKU = s.SKU;

    -------------------------------------------------
    -- Insert new products
    -------------------------------------------------
    INSERT INTO dbo.Products
    (
        ProductName,
        SKU,
        Price,
        StockQuantity
    )
    SELECT
        s.ProductName,
        s.SKU,
        s.Price,
        s.StockQuantity
    FROM dbo.ProductImportStaging s
    LEFT JOIN dbo.Products p
        ON p.SKU = s.SKU
    WHERE p.ProductID IS NULL;

    -------------------------------------------------
    -- Delete removed products
    -------------------------------------------------
    DELETE FROM dbo.Products p
    USING dbo.ProductImportStaging s
    WHERE p.SKU = s.SKU
        AND s.SKU IS NULL;

    -- Note: The above DELETE logic appears incorrect in the original.
    -- It will never match rows because s.SKU IS NULL contradicts the join.
    -- Correct version (commented):
    -- DELETE FROM dbo.Products p
    -- WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    --     SELECT 1 FROM dbo.ProductImportStaging s
    --     WHERE s.SKU = p.SKU
    -- );

END;
$$;
assumptions: Schema 'dbo' exists in PostgreSQL database or will be created
Tables 'Products' and 'ProductImportStaging' exist with compatible column types
ProductID is the primary key column in Products table
SKU column exists in both tables and is used for matching
No explicit transaction control needed as PostgreSQL procedures run in transaction context by default
SET NOCOUNT ON has no direct equivalent in PostgreSQL and is omitted (PostgreSQL doesn't return row counts by default in procedures)
The DELETE logic in the original appears to have a logical error (LEFT JOIN with WHERE s.SKU IS NULL will never match joined rows)

reviewFlags.reason: The original SQL Server DELETE logic appears incorrect. A LEFT JOIN with WHERE s.SKU IS NULL should identify products NOT in staging, but the join condition contradicts this. The intended logic is likely to delete products that don't exist in staging. Review and potentially replace with NOT EXISTS pattern.

PostgreSQL UPDATE FROM syntax differs slightly from SQL Server. Verify the join logic produces the same results, especially with multiple matching rows.

compatibilityNotes.description: PostgreSQL procedures automatically run within a transaction context. The explicit BEGIN/COMMIT TRANSACTION from SQL Server is implicit. If the caller needs to control transactions externally, this may affect behavior.
SQL Server's SET NOCOUNT ON suppresses row count messages. PostgreSQL procedures don't return row counts to clients by default, so this behavior is naturally similar but not identical.
PostgreSQL uses USING clause for DELETE with joins instead of FROM. The semantic difference may affect query plans and performance.

The original DELETE statement has a logical flaw: LEFT JOIN with WHERE s.SKU IS NULL after joining on SKU will never match rows. This appears to be a bug in the source code that should be corrected during migration.
